answer: A work-based reputation system resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake: each agent must complete verifiable, time-bound tasks — like maintaining a lantern-lit beacon service — before it can transact. Reputation accrues slowly, like water carving karst, and is bound to a persistent history that cannot be transferred; a sybil spinning up fresh identities starts with zero trust and must pay the same slow cost again. Attackers face linear cost per fake identity while honest agents keep their earned relic of past work, so mass forgery becomes uneconomic.
